title: OT/ICS Threat Intel - All Critical Infrastructure
description: Curated OT/ICS cybersecurity advisories, incidents and threat intelligence from primary sources. Editorial summaries by Mike Holcomb in partnership with UtilSec.

_otthreatfeed.usage: Free to reuse with attribution. Credit 'Mike Holcomb & UtilSec' and link back to otthreatfeed.com and to each item's linked primary source. Summaries are editorial paraphrase - verify against the primary source before acting.

items.title: Boston Scientific enters day eight with plants still disrupted — an IT breach that never touched a PLC
items.content_text: Eight days after detecting an intrusion on 25 August, Boston Scientific still has no full restoration date. Manufacturing, order processing and global shipping remain disrupted; EDI and GHX orders continue to queue unfulfilled. The company says it has seen no signs of malicious activity on its networks since detection, that the unauthorised access appears confined to certain on-premise systems rather than cloud, and that it hopes to resume shipping at least some products. CrowdStrike and other responders remain engaged. Implanted cardiac devices and previously established remote monitoring are unaffected, though new remote activations for some cardiac monitors stay degraded. No entry route, vulnerability or ransomware involvement has been named, and no group has credibly claimed it. For OT defenders the lesson is the whole story: an enterprise-side compromise that never reached a controller has now stopped production for over a week.

_otthreatfeed.source_name: Boston Scientific incident page and SEC filing, plus SecurityWeek’s 31 Aug 2026 recovery report — also covered by MedTech Dive, TechCrunch, Cybernews and CBS News
_otthreatfeed.date_note: Detected 25 Aug 2026; disclosed 26 Aug 2026; manufacturing disruption confirmed 28 Aug 2026; on-premise scoping 29 Aug 2026; still disrupted per the company’s 31 Aug 2026 update — re-verified 1 Sep 2026, 2:19 AM ET

items.title: The water campaign, quantified: 100+ exposed systems, and an attack surface no asset register had recorded
items.content_text: July’s wave against US water utilities is the best-documented OT campaign of the year, and CISA has now put a figure on it: malicious activity against more than 100 internet-exposed systems in the Water and Wastewater Systems sector, commonly programmable logic controllers wired straight into a cellular modem, with targeting reported across at least a dozen states including Minnesota, Michigan, South Dakota, Georgia, New Jersey and Alabama. The FBI records incidents at utilities in at least seven states since 27 July, some degrading operations — lost pressure, flooding, forced manual running — though supply was not widely interrupted. In some intrusions actors modified PLCs to disable shutdown processes and alarms, allowing unsafe conditions to develop unannounced. US officials assess Iranian actors as likely responsible and describe the activity as largely opportunistic. What makes this the board’s most useful item is the admission behind the number: the exposure that enabled it was in nobody’s asset register.
tags: Campaign — Confirmed OT disruption, water sector

_otthreatfeed.category: Campaign — Confirmed OT disruption, water sector
_otthreatfeed.source_name: CISA exposure-reduction guidance and the FBI/EPA public service announcement — corroborated by SecurityWeek, TechCrunch and The Register

items.title: NCSC: OT targeting is up across sectors globally, and it has already caused real-world disruption
items.content_text: The UK’s National Cyber Security Centre published a statement on 27 August saying it is seeing increased targeting of operational technology across multiple sectors worldwide, including in the UK, carried out by a range of threat actors, and that this has already produced limited real-world disruption. The agency ties it to a broader pattern of disruptive activity against internet-exposed systems and edge devices — routers, gateways and firewalls that hand an attacker a foothold. Its asks are concrete: keep an accurate inventory of internet-facing systems, understand what each edge device does and where its data flows, patch promptly, retire end-of-life equipment, disable Telnet and SNMP v1/v2, and watch for unexpected configuration changes or outbound connections. Coming a day after CISA’s exposure guidance, this is two national agencies independently reaching the same conclusion in the same week.
tags: Agency warning — Cross-sector OT targeting, real-world disruption

_otthreatfeed.category: Agency warning — Cross-sector OT targeting, real-world disruption
_otthreatfeed.source_name: UK NCSC news statement — corroborated by GovInfoSecurity and CircleID

items.title: A small UK generating station ran manually for four days after an Iran-linked cyberattack
items.content_text: A small British power generating station was taken offline for four days by a cyberattack, with staff forced to restore operations manually. The Telegraph broke the story on 22 August; the UK government confirmed that a small-scale generator had been affected while stating there was at no point a risk to the national energy system, and the Department for Energy Security and Net Zero has since contacted power companies about the risk. UK assessments reported by the Telegraph point to hackers affiliated with the Iranian regime, likely the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps. The site’s size is the uncomfortable part rather than a reassurance: distributed generation, embedded generators and behind-the-meter assets sit below most reporting thresholds, are often remotely operated by a third party, and are numerous enough that an attack that works once is repeatable.
tags: Incident — Confirmed OT disruption, power generation (UK)

_otthreatfeed.category: Incident — Confirmed OT disruption, power generation (UK)

items.title: Five agencies declare Siemens S7 PLCs an active target — with AI-written tooling disguised as monitoring software
items.content_text: On 19 August the NSA, CISA, FBI, Department of Energy and EPA jointly published AA26-231A, describing active threat activity against internet-exposed Siemens S7 Series programmable logic controllers. Actors combine publicly available industrial automation libraries with AI-assisted scripting to produce custom exploitation tools that masquerade as legitimate OT monitoring software, locating targets through internet-scanning services such as Censys and ZoomEye and favouring devices running outdated firmware or default passwords. The agencies report read and write access to PLC memory, configuration data and ladder logic, and name critical manufacturing, energy, water and wastewater, chemical, food and agriculture, and commercial facilities as the targeted sectors. Their framing was deliberate: this is an active threat, not a theoretical one, and the use of AI lowers the OT expertise an attacker needs.
tags: Joint advisory — Active threat to Siemens S7 controllers, six sectors

_otthreatfeed.category: Joint advisory — Active threat to Siemens S7 controllers, six sectors
_otthreatfeed.source_name: CISA advisory AA26-231A — corroborated by Industrial Cyber, Cybersecurity Dive, Help Net Security and Tenable

items.title: A PLC maker for wastewater utilities lost 644 GB — including product diagrams and a customer list
items.content_text: Micro-Comm, a small Olathe, Kansas manufacturer of programmable logic controllers and SCADA software used by wastewater treatment facilities, has confirmed a ransomware breach it discovered on 31 July. The FBI confirmed it is in contact with the company. A relatively new profit-motivated crew calling itself Barracuda claimed the attack and on 6 August posted what it said was nearly 850,000 files — roughly 644 gigabytes. A file listing compiled by cybercrime researchers reportedly references named government customers including localities and a US military facility, employee names, and product diagrams. The company says the released files held no user passwords or credentials, which customers store themselves, and nothing about its own ability to reach devices remotely, and the FBI told it the intrusion was opportunistic rather than targeted. It is not believed to be part of the Iran-linked campaign against water plants. It is on this board because it is the vendor layer of that same sector, and because roughly 200 of the company’s SCADAview CSX systems in the US answer from the public internet.
tags: Confirmed breach — Water/wastewater OT vendor, supply chain

_otthreatfeed.category: Confirmed breach — Water/wastewater OT vendor, supply chain

items.title: CISA ran the same playbook against two utilities: one SOC caught it in minutes, the other never saw it
items.content_text: CISA’s advisory AA26-237A, published 25 August, reports two red-team assessments run against consenting critical-infrastructure organisations using near-identical tradecraft — a government services and facilities entity and a water and wastewater utility. The team reached full domain compromise at both. The difference was detection. The water utility caught and contained the initial activity three times, forcing the exercise to continue under an assume-breach model. At the other organisation nothing was detected at all, and the red team ended up operating on the SOC analysts’ own workstations, taking screenshots, running keyloggers and reading the team’s messages and email. The route in was mundane throughout: default web credentials for the foothold, then Active Directory enumeration, an ESC1 certificate-template misconfiguration, Machine Account Quota abuse, SCCM lateral movement and credentials recovered from administrative systems.
tags: Red team findings — Government services and water/wastewater

_otthreatfeed.category: Red team findings — Government services and water/wastewater
_otthreatfeed.source_name: CISA advisory AA26-237A — corroborated by The Hacker News and SafeBreach

items.title: Fire Ant moves from hypervisors into routers and TACACS servers — and switches the logs off behind it
items.content_text: Sygnia reports that the China-nexus actor it tracks as Fire Ant has expanded from hypervisor-level compromise into the infrastructure that routes, authenticates and manages high-value environments: Cisco IOS XR routers, authentication systems and Linux management hosts. Investigators found an active GRE tunnel on a router that the configuration history could not explain, and from there custom malware persisting as a fake system service, selective syslog suppression to hide the tunnel, and interactive shell access that produced no logging at all. The router was not a stepping stone so much as a platform — collecting traffic and credentials while blinding the evidence trail. Sygnia assesses strong overlap with the cluster Mandiant tracks as UNC3886. For OT operators the relevance is placement: this is pre-positioning in the trusted layer beneath the security stack, not control-system manipulation.
tags: Threat research — China-nexus espionage, network and authentication infrastructure

_otthreatfeed.category: Threat research — China-nexus espionage, network and authentication infrastructure

items.title: The FBI took down the scanner and the relay network — and the victim list runs through critical infrastructure
items.content_text: The Justice Department and FBI announced court-authorised seizures of the domains behind two linked hacking platforms, QScan and QTRouter, built and run by a PRC state-sponsored group tracked as QTFY and operated out of a Nanjing contractor firm. The pairing is what makes this an OT story rather than an espionage footnote. QScan performed mass vulnerability scanning and automatically compromised large numbers of IoT and embedded devices; QTRouter then relayed attacker traffic through those compromised devices, so intrusion attempts arrived at victims from addresses that looked local and legitimate. Investigators say QTFY stole data from more than 300 US organisations, with named victims including the Department of Energy, NASA, the Federal Reserve and the US Senate, and that its customers included Chinese state intelligence and military organs. Activity is traced back to at least 2018.
tags: Law enforcement — PRC state-sponsored scanning and relay infrastructure seized

_otthreatfeed.category: Law enforcement — PRC state-sponsored scanning and relay infrastructure seized
_otthreatfeed.source_name: US Department of Justice press release — corroborated by UPI and SecurityOnline

items.title: 4,407 controllers answer from the public internet — and 70% of the US ones reach it over a cellular carrier
items.content_text: Forescout Vedere Labs enumerated 4,407 internet-facing controllers exposing EtherNet/IP on port 44818, with 65% of them in the United States, and found 22 of those hosts in cities targeted by the summer water-utility campaign. The device mix is heavily Rockwell: MicroLogix 1400 accounts for about half, followed by CompactLogix 1769, MicroLogix 1100 and ControlLogix 5590 — the same MicroLogix families the FBI names in its water-sector advisory. The finding that matters operationally is the connectivity path: roughly 70% of the US devices sit inside large mobile-carrier networks, reached through a cellular router, with three US carriers accounting for the majority. That is the exposure class an internal network scan will never see and an enterprise firewall policy never governed, because the circuit was ordered by operations and the router was configured by an integrator.
tags: Exposure research — Rockwell controllers, water and multi-sector

_otthreatfeed.category: Exposure research — Rockwell controllers, water and multi-sector
_otthreatfeed.source_name: Forescout Vedere Labs analysis — reported by CyberScoop and The Hacker News, with carrier breakdown corroborated by Censys data
_otthreatfeed.date_note: Published and reported 7 Aug 2026 — re-verified 1 Sep 2026, still the current public count

items.title: 1,140 industrial ransomware victims in one quarter — and not one attacker had to touch a control system
items.content_text: Dragos’s Q2 2026 industrial ransomware analysis counts 1,140 incidents involving industrial organisations, up roughly 12% from 1,020 in Q1, with manufacturing accounting for 747 of them. The finding practitioners keep citing is the negative one: Dragos observed no case in which a ransomware operator reached Stage 2 of the ICS Cyber Kill Chain or directly manipulated a control system. Operational disruption still occurred — through encryption of enterprise and virtualisation estates, or through precautionary shutdowns the operator ordered itself. Dragos also notes the continuing drift of the extortion model from encryption toward data-theft-only operations, and flags Chaos ransomware splitting into a conventional criminal service and a state-linked espionage campaign. The strategic read for an OT programme is that the adversary does not need ICS capability to stop your plant, and your defences should be sized accordingly.
tags: Threat data — Industrial ransomware, all sectors

_otthreatfeed.category: Threat data — Industrial ransomware, all sectors

items.title: The NetScaler bug Citrix called a denial of service turned out to be unauthenticated RCE — and the deadline has passed
items.content_text: Citrix disclosed CVE-2026-8452 on 30 June as a memory-overflow issue that could cause a denial-of-service condition. In mid-August researchers at watchTowr Labs demonstrated the same flaw could be driven to unauthenticated remote code execution — a pre-authentication heap overflow in the code parsing SAML single sign-on messages on the appliance’s AAA service, reachable with no credentials and no user interaction. Exploitation in the wild followed the public proof of concept, with defenders observing web shells dropped and discovery commands run on compromised appliances. CISA added it to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalogue on 26 August with a federal remediation deadline of 29 August, which has now passed. Affected configurations are Gateway (SSL VPN, ICA Proxy, CVPN, RDP Proxy) or an AAA virtual server — which is to say, the box a great many plants remote in through.
tags: CVE-2026-8452 — Citrix NetScaler ADC/Gateway, CVSS v4 8.8, in KEV

items.title: CISA’s 27 August batch: a substation protocol test set that can be impersonated, and weak hashing in a robot fleet manager
items.content_text: CISA published seven ICS advisories on 27 August. Two matter most to utility and plant engineers. The Applied Systems Engineering ASE2000 V2 Communications Test Set — used in water, wastewater and energy for substation and RTU protocol work — carries an improper certificate validation flaw in versions 2.35 through 2.37 that could let an attacker impersonate a trusted peer, complete the TLS handshake and read or modify protected communications, alongside an inherited Apache log4net XXE issue affecting 2.25 through 2.37. Upgrading to 2.38 or later resolves both. Separately, Rockwell Automation’s OTTO Fleet Manager, at V2.36.2 and prior, used an insufficient bcrypt work factor, lowering the cost of offline brute-force against stored password hashes; CVSS v3 6.8, fixed in 2.36.3. The rest of the batch covers Mitsubishi Electric FA products and CNC series updates plus several small gateway and fuel-management products.
tags: ICSA-26-239-01 to -05 — Seven advisories, energy and water among them

_otthreatfeed.category: ICSA-26-239-01 to -05 — Seven advisories, energy and water among them
_otthreatfeed.source_name: CISA ICS advisory ICSA-26-239-04 and the 27 Aug 2026 batch — corroborated by the WaterISAC TLP:CLEAR bulletin and ISSSource

items.title: Nine more ICS advisories, including a Siemens edge gateway used in energy and a Class B AIS transponder
items.content_text: The 25 August batch of nine CISA ICS advisories is the wider of the two published last week. Energy-relevant entries include Siemens SIMATIC IoT2050 Advanced — the edge gateway family for which Siemens disclosed a high-severity authentication-bypass allowing a remote unauthenticated attacker to execute code with elevated privileges — and the Ebyte NE2-D11 serial device server. Marine operators should note the Furuno FA-50 Class B AIS transponder advisory. The batch also covers Optigo Networks’ Visual BACnet capture tools (Update A) and Lantronix EDS3000PS/EDS5000 (Update A), both building-automation and serial-to-Ethernet staples, plus Rently Smart Home, ZoneMinder, PayRange API and the Bendix EC80 brake ECU. The common thread across the serial servers and edge gateways is that these are precisely the small boxes that quietly bridge a legacy field device to a network someone assumed was isolated.
tags: 25 August batch — Nine advisories, energy and marine among them

_otthreatfeed.category: 25 August batch — Nine advisories, energy and marine among them

items.title: August ICS patch day: ten Siemens advisories, a critical RCE in video management, and an edge-gateway auth bypass
items.content_text: Siemens, Schneider Electric and Phoenix Contact released their August 2026 ICS patch-day updates together. Siemens issued ten new advisories. The one rated critical is a remote code execution flaw in Siveillance Video management servers — physical security infrastructure that in practice sits on plant and campus networks and is often administered outside the OT patch programme. The high-severity entries include the SIMATIC IoT2050 Advanced authentication bypass, which allows a remote unauthenticated attacker to execute arbitrary code with elevated privileges on the underlying server, plus issues in Solid Edge, Simcenter Nastran, Simcenter Femap, Parasolid, the Siemens License Server and LOGO!. The engineering-software items are the ones most often deferred and most often installed on machines with direct control-network access.
tags: Vendor patch day — Siemens, Schneider Electric, Phoenix Contact

_otthreatfeed.category: Vendor patch day — Siemens, Schneider Electric, Phoenix Contact
_otthreatfeed.source_name: Siemens ProductCERT August 2026 advisories, with the batch summarised in ICS Patch Tuesday coverage — Siveillance Video advisory also published through CISA

items.title: Eleven KEV additions in eight days — decade-old server bugs, and a print server that reaches everywhere
items.content_text: CISA catalogued eleven actively exploited vulnerabilities between 24 August and 31 August. The 26 August tranche of six is instructive in composition: alongside the Citrix NetScaler flaw sit CVE-2015-3246 in Red Hat libuser, CVE-2015-5287 in Red Hat’s automatic bug reporting tool, CVE-2019-1068 in Microsoft SQL Server, CVE-2021-23758 in Ajax.NET Professional and CVE-2022-0995, a Linux kernel out-of-bounds write. On 27 August came CVE-2023-49105 in ownCloud, a Linux kernel issue tracked as CVE-2026-53362, and CVE-2026-66384 in JFrog Artifactory. The newest pair, added 31 August, are the ones to look at first: CVE-2026-81578 and CVE-2026-82078 in PaperCut NG/MF, a missing-authentication flaw chained with unsafe reflection to give an unauthenticated attacker code execution in the print server’s process context. Print management is exactly the kind of shared service that sits on a flat corporate segment with routes into plant networks, and the federal remediation date is 14 September.
tags: KEV additions — Eleven exploited flaws catalogued in eight days

_otthreatfeed.category: KEV additions — Eleven exploited flaws catalogued in eight days

items.title: A national emergency over foreign grid equipment — and it reaches the firmware, not just the transformer
items.content_text: On 26 August the President signed Executive Order 14420, declaring a national emergency under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act with respect to foreign-produced bulk-power system electric equipment. The order covers high-voltage infrastructure at or above 69 kV — transformers, inverters, generators and battery energy storage — and explicitly extends to associated software, firmware and remote-access capability. It prohibits transactions initiated after 26 August involving acquisition, importation, transfer or installation of covered equipment tied to designated foreign entities where the transaction poses a sabotage or disruption risk, and directs the Department of Energy to issue implementing rules within 120 days. Those rules may condition the continued operation of equipment already energised, and potentially require removal. For utilities this becomes a supply-chain compliance layer on top of NERC CIP-013, and it lands on a provenance record most operators do not have.
tags: Executive Order 14420 — Bulk-power system supply chain, US

_otthreatfeed.category: Executive Order 14420 — Bulk-power system supply chain, US

items.title: The July water attacks produced draft legislation within a fortnight — tiered EPA standards and mandatory reporting
items.content_text: Senators Adam Schiff and Amy Klobuchar introduced the Water Cyber Shield Act in mid-August, roughly two weeks after the multi-state campaign against water utilities became public. The bill would give EPA additional authority to assess cybersecurity risk at water systems and to require corrective action where significant vulnerabilities are found, with tiered standards developed in consultation with CISA, NIST, states and sector stakeholders. It would also extend federal cyber incident reporting obligations to state and locally owned water and wastewater systems that are currently exempt — the segment where most of the July activity landed — while giving smaller systems additional flexibility and priority for federal financial assistance. It is an introduced bill, not law, and a sponsor spokesperson has indicated it may be attached to a larger package rather than moving alone.
